title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks (arXiv:2305.06142v2)
summary: Problem: spatial and spectral GNNs build feature subspaces Phi_t = A^t X (or P_k(L)X) whose columns become increasingly linearly correlated with depth/order, and the weight-sharing mechanism plus thin node-attribute matrices (d << n) bound the representable feature space, hurting heterophilic graphs especially. Method: the paper decomposes GNNs into non-parametric feature spaces and trainable weights, then proposes FE-GNN, a purely linear model H = sum_k P_k(L)X W(k) + S Ws that (1) gives every feature subspace an independent weight matrix (feature subspace flattening) and (2) appends truncated-SVD structural principal components S of the normalized adjacency, with column-wise normalization of the whole feature space. Main result: under random 60/20/20 splits (100 runs, 10 seeds), FE-GNN (C)/(M) reach 73.33±0.35 / 73.26±0.38% on Chameleon and 67.82±0.26 / 67.90±0.23% on Squirrel (vs 61.85% / 47.21% for GCN), i.e., an average 32.0% improvement over GCN on three heterophilic datasets and +1.1% over ADA-UGNN on five homophilic datasets, at comparable per-epoch training time (~15.8 ms).

claims.statement: FE-GNN (C) (Chebyshev-polynomial Feature Expanded GNN) achieves 73.33% test accuracy (micro F1) on Chameleon node classification, mean over 100 runs with 95% CI ±0.35.

claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN (C): Chebyshev polynomial basis, order k=3; |S|=700 truncated-SVD components of normalized adjacency; hidden 64; lr 0.01; weight decay 0.0005 (Table 8 Chameleon row); column-wise normalized concatenated feature space; purely linear (no activation/dropout); Adam; early stopping warmup 50 / patience 200.

match_target.why: User hint: Table 2, FE-GNN (C) on Chameleon. This is the paper's headline result — the structural-principal-components modification on a heterophilic, limited-attribute graph — and it is the cheapest central claim to hit: one 2,277-node graph, a purely linear model, ~3 s per run and ~5 min for the full 100-run protocol on a single GPU (Table 4). C7 (GCN baseline) and C6 (w/o S ablation) serve as cheap sanity checks alongside it.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports a spread over repeated runs for this exact value — ±0.35, described as a 95% confidence interval over 100 runs on 10 random seeds (Table 2 / Sec. 6.1). Absolute band = 3 x 0.35 = 1.05, kept at the paper's printed precision (two decimals). (If the CI were first converted to a std via ±1.96σ the band would be ~0.54; we use the conservative direct reading of the reported spread. Note the test set is only ~456 of 2,277 nodes, so rule 2's 2,000+ example condition would not apply either.)

requirements.stmt: Implement the FE-GNN forward pass exactly as Eq. (11): H = sum_{k=0}^{K} P_k(Â)X W(k) + S·Ws, with one INDEPENDENT weight matrix per polynomial order plus one for the SVD subspace (no weight sharing across subspaces).
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses independent parameter matrices W (k) and Ws to reweight each feature subspace

requirements.stmt: Construct the structural principal components S by truncated SVD of the normalized structural matrix (S = Q̃Ṽ per Eq. (10)); for Chameleon keep |S|=700 components scaled by their singular values.
requirements.cite: Eq. (10), Sec. 4.2; Table 8 (|S|=700 for Chameleon); Sec. 6.2 (r=94% ratio rule)
requirements.quote: we propose to construct the expansion subspace using the truncated SVD of the structural matrix

requirements.stmt: Apply column-wise normalization so every column of the (concatenated) feature space has unit L2 norm before the weights are applied.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally

requirements.stmt: Keep the proposed model purely linear: no activation functions, no dropout; only the cross-entropy loss (unlike the baselines, whose non-linearity is preserved).
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: Use the renormalized adjacency Â = (D+I)^{-1/2}(A+I)(D+I)^{-1/2} and spectral matrix L̂ = I − Â as the structure matrices for the polynomial bases and the SVD.
Use polynomial order K=3 for Chameleon (Chebyshev basis for FE-GNN (C), monomial for FE-GNN (M)); the order ablation says order 3 is near-optimal.
requirements.cite: Table 8 (k=3 for Chameleon); Sec. 6.2 'At what order is a polynomial sufficient?'; Fig. 4
requirements.quote: This suggests that order 3 is good enough to achieve near-optimal performance

requirements.stmt: Load Chameleon through PyG and treat the graph as undirected (symmetrize edges) before computing Â and the SVD.
requirements.quote: We set these datasets to undirected graphs as we assumed in the Preliminaries.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with random 60%/20%/20% train/val/test node splits, 100 runs on 10 random seeds, reporting mean test accuracy with a 95% confidence interval.
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs in Table 2

requirements.stmt: Train with Adam; Chameleon hyperparameters lr=0.01, weight decay=0.0005, hidden=64 (Table 8); early stopping with warmup 50 and patience 200.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200
